description:
## [1.3.1](https://github.com/TahmidSummy/proxy-patches/compare/v1.3.0...v1.3.1) (2026-11-06)

### 🔒 Security

* **Proxy logins are no longer stored in the APK.** The **username** and **password** patch options have been removed.
  * Patch options are stored as plain text inside the patched APK, and **any app on your phone can read installed APKs**. That's how "APK extractor" apps work, with no root needed.
  * Your login is now only ever entered in the app: long-press the Reddit icon → **Proxy settings**. It's stored there in the app's private storage, which other apps can't read.
  * Host, port and proxy type remain available as patch options, to pre-fill the app.
* **Fixed a first-launch DNS leak.** Reddit has a startup "DNS warm-up" that, on a **fresh install's first launch**, looked up `gql-fed.reddit.com` and `cf.gql-fed.reddit.com` using your phone's own DNS, outside the proxy.
  * No traffic went around the proxy, but your network's DNS could see that you'd opened Reddit.
  * The warm-up is now switched off, and the proxy resolves those names as for everything else.

### 🐛 Bug fixes

* **No more false "Can't find your proxy's host name" at startup.** Reddit opens many connections at once when it starts, so a split-second DNS hiccup could fail several of them together and trigger the message, even though everything worked a moment later. A proxy problem now has to **last at least 8 seconds** before you're told about it. Real problems are still reported.

### ⚠️ After updating

* **If you had entered your proxy login as a patch option** (not in the app), enter it once in **Proxy settings**: long-press the Reddit icon. Until you do, the app tells you "Your proxy rejected the login".
* Logins already saved in the app's Proxy settings are kept, so there's nothing to do.

### ✅ Tested

Tested with Reddit 2026.40.0 on an Android 15 emulator, recording every connection **and every DNS lookup** the app made:

* **Fresh installs:** Reddit made **no DNS lookups of its own hostnames**, before and after setting a proxy.
* **Test HTTPS and SOCKS5 proxies:** everything went through the proxy. The only DNS lookup was the proxy's own name.
* **No login set:** the app stays offline and shows "Your proxy rejected the login".
* **Startup DNS hiccups:** no false proxy message any more.

### 📝 About encrypting the saved login

Encrypting the login inside the app (Android Keystore) was looked at and **not added for now**. Android already keeps it private from other apps, encrypts your phone's storage, and encrypts cloud backups with your screen lock. Malware with root could unlock it anyway. And it would add ways for the app to lose your login (for example after some system updates). This may be revisited if the patch ever stores anything more sensitive than a proxy login.

([a0f7bd0](https://github.com/TahmidSummy/proxy-patches/commit/a0f7bd0851f41c0756a3b0a37c5752bd0a3fa11e))
